newsitem.title: USA: Senate conferees reject House de minimis overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Senate conferees reject House de minimis overhaul.

text.p: The first counteroffer by U.S. senators negotiating the tax bill with the House of Representatives does not agree to the House's plan to scale back the two-percent de minimis rule, a Senate document shows.

The development is good news for the municipal bond market, whose issuers and dealers strongly oppose the House plan to radically cut back the de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of municipal bonds to a flat $1 million.
Lawmakers are trying to iron out differences in tax cut bills passed by the Senate and House to craft a single bill.

House conferees had started the negotiating process on Tuesday with a 27-page offer that included few concessions to senators. House conferees, for example, refused to back off from their call for a de minimis scaleback.
Negotiations between the House and Senate are continuing.
